name: Population
quote: A population consists of the entire set of individuals or objects that you want to learn about.
plain_en: every individual or object of interest

name: Sample
quote: A sample is a subset of the population that is selected for study.
plain_en: the part of a population studied

name: Statistics
quote: The field of statistics is all about collecting, describing, analyzing, and drawing conclusions from data.
plain_en: science of collecting and analyzing data

name: Parameter
quote: A parameter is a numerical summary of a population, while a statistic is a numerical summary of sample data.
plain_en: numerical summary of a whole population

name: Statistic
quote: A parameter is a numerical summary of a population, while a statistic is a numerical summary of sample data.
plain_en: numerical summary calculated from sample data

name: Conclusion in context
quote: Conclusions should be given in context, that is, should refer back to the population in a real-world frame of reference.
plain_en: answer stated in the real-world setting

name: Data
quote: Data are pieces of information about observational units (items or individuals).
plain_en: information recorded about individuals or objects

name: Observational unit
quote: Data are pieces of information about observational units (items or individuals).
plain_en: item or individual being studied

name: Variables
quote: Variables are characteristics that may change from one observational unit to another.
plain_en: characteristics that can vary between units

name: Categorical variable
quote: A categorical variable (or qualitative variable) places individuals into groups called categories.
plain_en: variable placing individuals into groups

name: Qualitative variable
quote: A categorical variable (or qualitative variable) places individuals into groups called categories.
plain_en: variable describing a category or group

name: Quantitative variable
quote: A quantitative variable (or numerical variable) takes on values for a measurable quantity.
plain_en: variable measuring a numerical quantity

name: Frequency table
quote: The values taken on by categorical variables can be organized into frequency tables or relative frequency tables.
plain_en: table counting values in each category

name: Relative frequency table
quote: The values taken on by categorical variables can be organized into frequency tables or relative frequency tables.
plain_en: table showing proportions in each category

name: Frequency
quote: Frequency gives the number of cases falling into each category, while relative frequency gives the proportion or percent of cases falling into each category.
plain_en: number of cases in a category

name: Relative frequency
quote: Frequency gives the number of cases falling into each category, while relative frequency gives the proportion or percent of cases falling into each category.
plain_en: proportion of cases in a category

name: Distribution
quote: The distribution of a variable describes the possible values the variable could assume and how often each of those values occurs.
plain_en: possible values and how often they occur

name: Bar chart
quote: They can be represented graphically by displays such as bar charts (bar graphs) and pie charts.
plain_en: graph with bars for categories

name: Pie chart
quote: They can be represented graphically by displays such as bar charts (bar graphs) and pie charts.
plain_en: circle divided into category slices

name: Discrete quantitative variable
quote: A discrete quantitative variable takes on a finite or countable number of values.
plain_en: countable numerical variable with gaps

name: Continuous quantitative variable
quote: A continuous quantitative variable can take on uncountable or infinite values with no gaps, such as heights and weights of students.
plain_en: numerical variable taking any value in an interval

name: Histogram
quote: Histograms, which are useful for large data sets involving quantitative variables, show frequencies or relative frequencies with bars over intervals called bins.
plain_en: bars showing frequencies over intervals

name: Bin
quote: Histograms, which are useful for large data sets involving quantitative variables, show frequencies or relative frequencies with bars over intervals called bins.
plain_en: interval used for histogram bars

name: Dotplot
quote: A quantitative variable takes on numerical values for a measured or counted quantity. The values can be organized into frequency tables or relative frequency tables or can be represented graphically by displays such as dotplots, histograms, stemplots, cumulative relative frequency plots, or boxplots.
plain_en: graph with dots for each value

name: Stemplot
quote: An alternative pictorial display, called a stemplot (also called a stem and leaf display), retains this individual information and is useful for giving a quick overview of a distribution, displaying the relative density and shape of the data.
plain_en: display splitting each value into stem and leaf

name: Ogive
quote: Sometimes we sum frequencies and show the result visually in a cumulative relative frequency plot (also known as an ogive).
plain_en: graph of cumulative relative frequencies

name: SOCS
quote: When describing a distribution, always comment on Shape, Outliers, Center, and Spread (SOCS).
plain_en: shape, outliers, center, and spread

name: Symmetric distribution
quote: A symmetric distribution is one in which the two halves are mirror images of each other.
plain_en: distribution with mirror-image halves

name: Skewed right
quote: A distribution is skewed to the right if it spreads far and thinly toward the higher values.
plain_en: distribution with a long right tail

name: Skewed left
quote: A distribution is skewed to the left if it spreads far and thinly toward the lower values.
plain_en: distribution with a long left tail

name: Bell-shaped distribution
quote: A bell-shaped distribution is symmetric with a center mound and two sloping tails.
plain_en: symmetric distribution with a central mound

name: Uniform distribution
quote: A distribution is uniform if its histogram is a horizontal line.
plain_en: distribution with equally likely values

name: Unimodal
quote: A distribution with one main peak is called unimodal and with two distinct peaks is called bimodal.
plain_en: distribution with one main peak

name: Bimodal
quote: A distribution with one main peak is called unimodal and with two distinct peaks is called bimodal.
plain_en: distribution with two distinct peaks

name: Outliers
quote: Outliers are values that are unusually small or large relative to the rest of the data.
plain_en: values far from the rest of the data

name: Gaps
quote: Gaps show holes where no values fall.
plain_en: intervals with no data values

name: Clusters
quote: Clusters show natural subgroups into which the values fall.
plain_en: natural subgroups of data values

name: Center
quote: The center either separates the values (or the area under the curve in a histogram) roughly in half (the median) or is calculated as an average (the mean).
plain_en: typical middle value of a distribution

name: Spread
quote: The spread or variability is the scope of the values from smallest to largest.
plain_en: range of values from smallest to largest

name: Median
quote: The median, which is the middle number of a set of numbers arranged in numerical order.
plain_en: middle value when data are ordered

name: Mean
quote: The mean, which is found by summing items in a set and dividing by the number of items.
plain_en: sum of values divided by count

name: Resistant measure
quote: The median and IQR are called resistant or robust measures because outliers do not greatly (if at all) affect their values.
plain_en: measure not greatly affected by outliers

name: Nonresistant measure
quote: The mean, range, variance, and standard deviation are called nonresistant or nonrobust measures because outliers can greatly affect their values.
plain_en: measure strongly affected by outliers

name: Five-number summary
quote: To understand variability, we either calculate the mean and standard deviation (defined below) or calculate the following five-number summary of a data set:
plain_en: minimum, Q1, median, Q3, maximum

name: First quartile (Q1)
quote: The 25th percentile, Q1, is the median of the lower half of the data set.
plain_en: median of the lower half of data

name: Third quartile (Q3)
quote: The 75th percentile, Q3, is the median of the upper half of the data set.
plain_en: median of the upper half of data

name: Range
quote: Range: the difference between the largest and smallest values (maximum minus minimum).
plain_en: maximum value minus minimum value

name: Interquartile range (IQR)
quote: Interquartile range (IQR): the difference between the largest and smallest values after removing the lower and upper quartiles.
plain_en: spread of the middle half of data

name: Variance
quote: Variance: the average of the squared differences from the mean.
plain_en: average squared distance from the mean

name: Standard deviation
quote: Standard deviation (SD): the square root of the variance.
plain_en: typical distance of values from the mean

name: 1.5 × IQR rule
quote: The more common rule is that outliers are any value less than Q1 – 1.5(IQR) or greater than Q3 + 1.5(IQR).
plain_en: rule flagging values beyond 1.5 IQR

name: Simple ranking
quote: Simple ranking, which involves arranging the elements in some order and noting where in that order a particular value falls.
plain_en: position of a value in an ordered list

name: Percentile ranking
quote: Percentile ranking, which indicates what percentage of all values fall at or below the value under consideration.
plain_en: percent of values at or below a value

name: z-score
quote: The z-score, which states very specifically the number of standard deviations a particular value is above or below the mean.
plain_en: number of standard deviations from the mean

name: Quartiles
quote: Quartiles split data into four equal parts.
plain_en: values dividing data into four parts

name: Deciles
quote: Deciles split data into 10 equal parts.
plain_en: values dividing data into ten parts

name: Boxplot
quote: A boxplot (also called a box and whisker display) is a visual representation displaying the distribution of data that shows the smallest value, the largest value, the middle (median), the middle of the bottom half of the set (Q1), and the middle of the top half of the set (Q3).
plain_en: display showing five-number summary and outliers

name: Comparing distributions
quote: When asked for a comparison, don’t forget to address Shape, Unusual features (Outliers, gaps, clusters), Center, and Spread (SOCS or CUSS) and to refer to context.
plain_en: describe shape, outliers, center, and spread comparatively

name: Investigative question
quote: There are three principal components to the investigative question:
plain_en: question a study is designed to answer

name: Random sample
quote: A sample is considered random when all observational units in the sample are selected from the population using some type of random mechanism.
plain_en: sample selected using chance

name: Randomization in sampling
quote: The use of randomization in sample selection increases the chance that the resulting sample exhibits all the known and unknown features of the population.
plain_en: using chance to select a sample

name: Generalizability
quote: A sample is generalizable only to the population from which the sample was selected.
plain_en: applying sample results only to its population

name: Observational study
quote: In an observational study, we simply observe and measure something that has taken place or is taking place while trying not to cause any changes by our presence.
plain_en: study observing without imposing a treatment

name: Experiment
quote: In an experiment, we impose some change or treatment and measure the response.
plain_en: study imposing a treatment and measuring response

name: Cause-and-effect conclusion
quote: It is not possible to conclude a cause-and-effect relationship between variables using data collected from an observational study.
plain_en: concluding one variable causes another

name: Blocking
quote: If there is an important difference among the subjects, similar subjects should be grouped into blocks, and treatments should be randomized within the blocks.
plain_en: grouping similar subjects before random treatment

name: Observational studies
quote: Observational studies aim to gather information about a population without disturbing the population.
plain_en: studies observing a population undisturbed

name: Retrospective study
quote: Retrospective studies look backward, examining existing data, while prospective studies watch for outcomes, tracking individuals into the future.
plain_en: study examining existing past data

name: Prospective study
quote: Retrospective studies look backward, examining existing data, while prospective studies watch for outcomes, tracking individuals into the future.
plain_en: study tracking individuals into the future

name: Sampling variability
quote: Different samples give different statistics, all of which are estimates for the same population parameter.
plain_en: statistics varying from sample to sample

name: Census
quote: Collecting data from every individual in a population, called a census, might seem to provide complete information, but unless the population is small, this method would be prohibitively expensive and time-consuming.
plain_en: attempt to measure an entire population

name: Sampling frame
quote: The list of all individuals from which the sample is drawn is called the sampling frame.
plain_en: list from which a sample is drawn

name: Simple random sample (SRS)
quote: A simple random sample (SRS) is one in which every possible sample of the desired size has an equal chance of being selected.
plain_en: sample where every sample size n is equally likely

name: Stratified random sampling
quote: Stratified random sampling involves dividing the population into non-overlapping homogeneous groups called strata, then picking random samples from each of the strata, and finally combining these individual samples into what is called a stratified random sample.
plain_en: random samples from homogeneous subgroups

name: Strata
quote: Stratified random sampling involves dividing the population into non-overlapping homogeneous groups called strata, then picking random samples from each of the strata, and finally combining these individual samples into what is called a stratified random sample.
plain_en: homogeneous subgroups of a population

name: Proportional sampling
quote: We could further do proportional sampling, where the sizes of the random samples from each stratum depend on the proportion of the total population represented by the stratum.
plain_en: stratum sample sizes matched to population proportions

name: Cluster random sampling
quote: Cluster random sampling involves dividing the population into non-overlapping heterogeneous groups called clusters, each similar to each other, and then picking everyone or everything in a random selection of one or more of the clusters.
plain_en: sample whole randomly chosen heterogeneous groups

name: Systematic random sampling
quote: Systematic random sampling is a relatively simple and quick method. It involves listing the population in some order (for example, alphabetically), choosing a random point to start, and then picking every tenth (or hundredth, or thousandth, or kth) person from the list.
plain_en: choose random start then every kth unit

name: Sampling for homogeneity
quote: However, sometimes we instead randomly pick a sample from each of two or more populations and then compare the distribution of some variable among the different populations. This second method is called sampling for homogeneity.
plain_en: random samples from several populations compared

name: Sampling bias
quote: A sampling method is biased if in some critical way it consistently results in samples that do not represent the population.
plain_en: method consistently producing unrepresentative samples

name: Voluntary response survey
quote: Voluntary response surveys are based on individuals who choose to participate
plain_en: survey of people who choose to respond

name: Convenience survey
quote: Convenience surveys are based on choosing individuals who are easy to reach
plain_en: survey using easily reached individuals

name: Undercoverage bias
quote: Undercoverage bias happens when there is inadequate representation, and thus some groups in the population are left out of the process of choosing the sample.
plain_en: some population groups left out of sampling

name: Response bias
quote: Response bias occurs when the question itself can lead to misleading results because people don’t want to be perceived as having unpopular or unsavory views or don’t want to admit to having committed crimes.
plain_en: question wording leads to misleading answers

name: Nonresponse bias
quote: Nonresponse bias, where there are low response rates, occurs when individuals chosen for the sample can’t be contacted or refuse to participate, and it is often unclear which part of the population is responding.
plain_en: bias from people refusing to respond

name: Experimental unit
quote: An experiment is performed on objects called experimental units.
plain_en: object on which an experiment is performed

name: Subject
quote: If the units are people, they are called subjects.
plain_en: person participating in an experiment

name: Factor
quote: Experiments involve explanatory variables, called factors, that are believed to have an effect on response variables.
plain_en: explanatory variable in an experiment

name: Response variable
quote: A group is intentionally treated with some level of the explanatory variable, and the outcome of the response variable is measured.
plain_en: outcome measured in an experiment

name: Comparison
quote: In comparison, we wish to compare a response variable with regard to two or more experimental conditions (treatments)
plain_en: comparing responses across treatments

name: Control group
quote: If the purpose of an experiment is to determine whether some treatment has an effect, we compare to a control group that doesn’t receive that treatment.
plain_en: group not receiving the treatment

name: Placebo
quote: Depending on the experiment, a control group may be given an inactive treatment (a placebo), an established active treatment, or no treatment at all.
plain_en: inactive dummy treatment

name: Blinding
quote: Blinding occurs when the subjects don’t know which of the different treatments (such as placebos) they are receiving.
plain_en: subjects unaware of treatment received

name: Double-blinding
quote: Double-blinding is when neither the subjects nor the response evaluators know who is receiving which treatment.
plain_en: subjects and evaluators unaware of treatments

name: Random assignment
quote: In random assignment, we use chance to randomly assign treatments to experimental units:
plain_en: using chance to assign treatments

name: Replication
quote: In replication, the larger the sample is, the more significant the observation:
plain_en: using enough subjects in each treatment

name: Control
quote: Control allows us to minimize the sources of variation other than the treatments by making conditions as similar as possible for all treatment groups:
plain_en: keeping conditions similar across groups

name: Confounding
quote: Two variables are confounded when both are associated with a response variable and are also associated with each other.
plain_en: two variables effects cannot be separated

name: Completely randomized design
quote: Random assignment to treatments, called completely randomized design, is critical in good experimental design.
plain_en: all subjects randomly assigned to treatments

name: Matched pairs design
quote: A matched pairs design (also called a paired comparison design) is when two treatments are compared based on the responses of paired subjects, one of whom receives one treatment while the other receives the second treatment.
plain_en: treatments compared using paired subjects
covers_concepts: Matched pairs design; Paired comparison design

name: Block design
quote: blocking, in experimental design, first divides the subjects into representative groups called blocks based on similar characteristics. Subjects within each block are randomly assigned treatments.
plain_en: randomize treatments within similar blocks

name: Statistically significant
quote: something is statistically significant if the probability of it happening just by chance is so small that you’re convinced there must be another explanation.
plain_en: result unlikely to occur by chance alone

name: Bias
quote: Bias: when a study systematically favors certain outcomes
plain_en: study systematically favors certain outcomes

name: Block design (glossary)
quote: Block design: an experimental design where subjects are divided into representative groups to bring certain differences into the picture and reduce variation (for example, blocking by gender, age, or race) and randomization then takes place within each block
plain_en: divide subjects into groups then randomize

name: Explanatory variable
quote: Experiments involve explanatory variables, called factors, that are believed to have an effect on response variables.
plain_en: variable thought to affect the response
